findings.comment: Provide dimensioned clearances from all four transformer pads to adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, and structures per UCM § 1.10.4 requirements (10 feet for hot-stick use area, 5 feet for sides with operators/controls, 3-5 feet for other sides depending on building construction type). Confirm building construction types if any clearances are less than standard requirements.
applicableAreas: Four transformer pad locations on the site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies four locations labeled "Electrical Transformer Pad": (1) west of Building 1 near Unit 101, (2) west of Building 8 near Unit 801, (3) south of Building 5 near Unit 504, and (4) north of Building 7 near Unit 705. All four pads are shown as simple squares with no dimension lines showing clearances to adjacent buildings, parking areas, walkways, or structures. The site plan shows driveways and parking areas in close proximity to these pads, but no distances are dimensioned.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies clearance requirements for pad-mounted equipment based on the type of adjacent structures and whether the equipment has operator/control access. Required clearances range from 3 feet (non-operator sides, non-brick/masonry buildings) to 10 feet (hot-stick use area). The absence of dimensioned clearances prevents verification that the design complies with these minimum setbacks and prevents determination of whether reduced clearances (3 feet instead of 5 feet) require AE Design written approval per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2. Building construction type (brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating vs. non-brick/masonry) must be documented to determine which clearance column in Table 1.10.4 applies.

findings.comment: Clearances from the four transformer pads are not shown or dimensioned on any plan sheets. Design must provide UCM § 1.10.4 compliant clearances (10 ft hot-stick area, 5 ft operator areas, 3 ft other sides) dimensioned from each pad to buildings, parking, driveways, and other obstructions. Building construction type (brick/masonry 2-hour fire-rated vs. non-brick/masonry) must be documented to determine applicable clearance table.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8; near parking areas and driveways
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads with generic labels only ('Electrical Transformer Pad') and no specifications (kVA ratings, dimensions, or type). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) displays the same transformer locations in spatial context with buildings, driveways, parking spaces, and sidewalks. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that no clearance dimensions or lines are dimensioned from any transformer pad to nearby buildings, parking areas, driveways, or sidewalks. The drawing shows relationships graphically but provides zero quantitative clearance verification.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies clearance requirements from pad-mounted equipment: minimum 10 feet on hot-stick use area (side with door), 5 feet on sides with operators/controls, and 3 feet on sides without operators/controls (from removable ventilated obstructions). Additionally, buildings affect these clearances—non-brick/masonry buildings trigger the standard clearances; brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating allows reduced clearances. No building construction types are documented, and no clearance dimensions are shown from the transformers to any adjacent structures. The plans cannot demonstrate compliance with Table 1.10.4 without these dimensions and without knowledge of building construction type.

findings.comment: Transformer pad clearances from buildings, parking areas, sidewalks, and other structures not shown or dimensioned on electrical design plan. Provide dimensioned clearance details for both transformer pads per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 (minimum 3 feet to 10 feet depending on side and building type), including verification of building construction type (brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating vs. non-brick/masonry) for clearance determination.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts two transformer pads on the site plan drawing. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that no dimensions or clearance radii are labeled for either transformer pad. The pads are drawn in proximity to parking areas, driveways, and building footprints, but no specific clearance distances are dimensioned or noted. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the overall layout with buildings and parking areas but provides no transformer pad clearance dimensions. The preliminary electrical plan shows the general locations of the two transformer pads but provides no evidence of compliance with the minimum clearance requirements specified in UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 (10 ft hot-stick use area, 5 ft sides with operators/controls, 3 ft other sides based on building type and fire rating).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires specific clearances from pad-mounted equipment based on the side of the equipment and building construction type. The required clearances range from 3 feet to 10 feet depending on the side and building characteristics. The applicant's burden is to demonstrate compliance through dimensioned drawings. The absence of any clearance dimensions or notes on the electrical plan and site plan means the requirement cannot be verified. The deficiency is not that compliance might not exist in reality, but that the required documentation is absent. The preliminary design nature of the electrical plan (labeled as 'Preliminary Electrical Design') combined with the complete absence of clearance dimensions indicates this item must be addressed with detailed clearance callouts and notes before the design can be verified as compliant.

findings.comment: Transformer pad locations shown on Sheet 21 do not include dimensioned clearances to adjacent buildings, parking areas, sidewalks, or other features. Add dimensions to all transformer pads showing clearances to: adjacent buildings (minimum 10-15 feet per UCM § 1.10.4), parking/traffic areas (maximum 6 feet, with bollards if less than 4 feet), windows and doors (minimum 5-12 feet per orientation), and fire escapes/stairs (minimum 20 feet if oil-filled equipment). Verify all clearances meet Table 1.10.4 requirements.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts three electrical transformer pads: one west of Building 2/northwest of Building 8 near the western property line and street entrance; one between Buildings 8 and 6 in the central driveway/alley area; and one east of Building 5 near the eastern property boundary. The vision analysis confirmed: 'There are no specific dimensions (e.g., distance lines with measurements) provided on this sheet to indicate the exact clearances from the transformer pads to the buildings, doors, or windows.' No clearance dimensions are shown from any transformer pad to: adjacent buildings (Buildings 2, 5, 6, 8), building doors or windows, parking areas, sidewalks, or fire escapes. No dimensions verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requirements: 10 feet minimum for hot-stick use area to adjacent building, 15 feet if facing confined space, 20 feet from oil-filled equipment to fire escape/stairs, 5 feet lateral or 12 feet vertical from windows/doors, 6 feet maximum from parking/traffic areas for truck access, or bollard locations if within 4 feet of parking.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.27 specifies 'Proposed buildings, bike racks, or site features do not meet required safety clearances from Austin Energy facilities' and applies 'Only when site is adjacent to Austin Energy facilities requiring safety clearances.' The grouping instruction requires 'Check: Site plan dimensions, Austin Energy equipment locations (transformers, vaults), clearance compliance per Table 1.10.4 (10 ft to 20 ft depending on configuration).' UCM § 1.10.4 establishes specific minimum clearances from pad-mounted transformers and distribution equipment based on configuration and adjacent features. The site has three transformer pads shown on the electrical plan with buildings, parking, and sidewalks in close proximity. Without dimensioned clearances on the site plan, it cannot be verified that any of the proposed transformer locations comply with the safety clearance requirements of UCM § 1.10.4. The preliminary nature of the design and absence of clearance documentation means compliance is unverified.

findings.comment: Clearance conflicts between proposed buildings and transmission facilities not documented or dimensioned. Coordinate with Austin Energy Transmission C&M (per Sheet 3 Block 20 note: contact Andrew Perez 512-505-7153) to confirm building locations maintain required clearances from transmission poles/structures. Add clearance dimensions to site and electrical plans showing compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 and transmission facility requirements (25 feet from transmission structures, proper staging area clearances, etc.). Include Austin Energy clearance verification documentation on final plans.
applicableAreas: proposed buildings and site features adjacent to transmission facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Block 20 contains detailed 'Electric Transmission Notes' with 16 items specifying clearance requirements and restrictions for transmission facilities on the property. These notes reference no digging/grading within 25 feet of transmission structures, minimum clearances from aerial equipment and staging areas, road/driveway load requirements for easement areas, and prohibitions on structures in transmission easement. The transmission notes indicate transmission facilities are present and active on or immediately adjacent to the site. However, Sheet 21 (Electrical Site Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) do not show clearance dimensions between the proposed buildings (Bldgs 1-8) and transmission structures or indicate how the 25-foot no-dig/no-grade clearance has been maintained around any transmission poles or structures. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 found transformer pads and buildings depicted but no clearance annotations or dimensions between buildings and transmission facilities. The site plan does not show transmission pole or structure locations, making it impossible to verify from the documents whether buildings and site features meet the required clearances (e.g., 10 ft for hot-stick use area per UCM § 1.10.4 Table, 20 ft for oil-filled equipment to fire escapes per grouping narrative).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 establishes minimum clearances from Austin Energy equipment. Sheet 3 Block 20 demonstrates that transmission facilities are present on/adjacent to the site, requiring compliance with transmission facility clearances (25 feet no-dig, 20 feet for aerial equipment, etc.). Sheet 21 does not show transmission structure locations or clearance dimensions between buildings and transmission infrastructure. Without documented verification that buildings and site features maintain required clearances from transmission facilities, compliance cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Add clearance dimensions to the electrical site plan for each of the four transformer pad locations per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4. For each pad, dimension the clearances to: adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, pedestrian walkways, fencing, mail kiosks, and any other site features. Specify clearances in feet (minimum 5-20 feet depending on configuration). Indicate bollard locations if pads are within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. Specify sidewalk setback (minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalk) and truck access route (minimum 6 feet adjacent clearance). Add notes confirming compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads and clearances to buildings, parking, and site features
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pad locations: (1) northwest corner near Building 1, (2) between Buildings 2 and 8, (3) between Buildings 4 and 5, and (4) between Buildings 6 and 7. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts these transformer pads in relation to buildings and parking areas. However, visual analysis of Sheet 21 found 'absolutely no dimensions, dashed clearance lines, or safety zones drawn or annotated around any of this equipment.' Similarly, analysis of Sheet 9 found 'no explicit clearance or setback dimensions shown between the Transformer Pad and the adjacent buildings, parking areas, or other site features.' UCM § 1.10.4 establishes specific minimum clearances for pad-mounted transformers and distribution vaults ranging from 5 feet to 20 feet depending on configuration and adjacent features.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 establishes mandatory minimum clearances from pad-mounted transformers: (1) Hot-stick use area (pad-locked sides) to adjacent building/structure: minimum 10 feet; (2) Hot-stick use area facing confined space (niche/vault): minimum 15 feet; (3) Oil-filled equipment to fire escape/stairs: minimum 20 feet horizontal/radial clearance; (4) Adjacent to brick/masonry building (2-hour fire rating): minimum 5 feet from side edges; (5) Adjacent to non-brick/masonry building: minimum 12 feet from oil-filled equipment; (6) Windows, doors, ventilating ducts: 5 feet lateral or 12 feet vertical if lateral less than 5 feet; (7) Equipment pads within 6 feet from parking/traffic areas must have truck access, and bollards required if within 4 feet; (8) Transformer pads must be 2 feet from back of sidewalks. The electrical site plan must show all four transformer locations with clearance dimensions to all adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, walkways, and fencing to demonstrate compliance. The absence of any clearance dimensions is the deficiency.

findings.comment: Transformer pad locations are shown on electrical design plan but distances to parking/traffic areas are not dimensioned. Bollard protection details are not shown. Verification required that all pads are either more than 4 feet from parking/traffic or that 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards are detailed per UCM § 1.10.4.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations near parking areas
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design) shows 4 transformer pads located at: west side near entrance drive (landscape island), southwest area near entrance (landscape island), east side central area (between Bldg. 4 and 5), and southeast area (between Bldg. 6 and 7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 10 surface parking spaces and 78 garage parking spaces, with surface parking primarily concentrated in the central entrance area and along the main drive aisles. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 indicated that 'None of the transformer pads appear to be within 4 feet of designated parking stalls' based on visual inspection, but the analysis noted the lack of explicit distance dimensions on the plan. Without precise distance measurements between the transformer pads and the nearest parking stalls/traffic areas, and without bollard details shown on the electrical plan, it cannot be definitively confirmed whether the 4-foot minimum clearance requirement is met at all locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that pad-mounted equipment within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas must have 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards per AE Design equipment pad details. The site plan shows transformer locations and parking areas but does not provide dimensioned distances from pads to parking/traffic edges. While vision analysis suggested pads are not immediately adjacent to parking stalls, the lack of explicit distance callouts and the absence of any bollard details on the electrical plan create ambiguity. The requirement applies if pads are within 4 feet, but precise verification requires either: (1) detailed measurements on the plan, or (2) explicit notation that clearance exceeds 4 feet. No bollard details are shown on Sheet 21.

findings.comment: Bollards not shown when equipment pads are within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas. Add 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards around each transformer pad per Austin Energy Design equipment pad details. Show bollard locations and spacing on site plan with reference to AE Design standard details.
applicableAreas: Middle areas adjacent to drive aisles
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads (dashed rectangles) at locations middle-left (west of Bldg 1), bottom-left (west of Bldg 8), middle-right (between Bldgs 4-5), and bottom-right (between Bldgs 6-7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows these transformer pads immediately adjacent to internal drive aisles (parking and traffic areas). No bollards, protective barriers, or any protective posts are shown around any of the transformer pad locations. No callouts or notes reference bollard requirements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) per AE Design equipment pad details when pad-mounted equipment is within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. The transformer pads shown on Sheet 9 are positioned directly adjacent to internal drive aisles and parking areas, placing them well within the 4-foot proximity threshold. The absence of bollards on all four transformer pads is a deficiency. Bollards are essential to protect pad-mounted transformers from vehicle damage.

findings.comment: Transformer 3 is located within 4 feet of surface parking and drive aisle but no bollards are shown. Provide 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollard posts per AE Design equipment pad details, positioned to protect the transformer pad from vehicular impact and maintain required clearances.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) depicts three transformer pads. Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) confirms that Transformer 3 (located between Buildings 6 and 7 on the east side of the site) is positioned within a paved area with surface parking spaces to the northwest and the main concrete drive aisle immediately adjacent. The transformer is clearly within 4 feet of parking and traffic circulation areas. Sheet 21 shows the transformer pad symbol but contains no indication of bollards, protective posts, or any barrier/protection device at this location. No detail sheet (Sheets 22-39) provides bollard details for this transformer location.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) per AE Design equipment pad details for pad-mounted equipment located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. Transformer 3 is clearly within 4 feet of surface parking spaces and a paved drive aisle. The absence of bollards shown on the electrical plan or detail sheets indicates this requirement has not been addressed. Bollards are required to protect the transformer pad from vehicular impact and to maintain safe clearance from traffic.

findings.comment: Multiple transformer pads appear to be located within 2 feet of concrete sidewalks per visual analysis of Sheet 9. Provide: (1) Updated site plan with dimension lines and callouts clearly documenting the distance from back of sidewalk to each transformer pad (T1, T2, T3, T4), confirming minimum 2-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.4, OR (2) Reposition transformers to achieve minimum 2-foot separation from all sidewalks, or (3) If clearance cannot be achieved, provide documented approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing reduced sidewalk clearance with specific approval conditions.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pads (T1, T2, T3, T4) relative to adjacent sidewalks and pedestrian paths
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to measure distance from transformer pads to sidewalks and pedestrian paths. Vision analysis identified clearances for each transformer: 'T1: A Concrete Sidewalk wraps tightly around the eastern and northern sides of this pad. It appears to be within 2 feet of the pad. T2: A concrete sidewalk running north-south along the side of Bldg. 4 passes very close to the western edge of this pad (appears to be within 2 feet). T3: A concrete walkway runs east-west just north of the pad, connecting the driveway to Unit 604. It appears to be within 2 to 5 feet. T4: A concrete sidewalk runs north-south just to the east of the pad, leading to Unit 801. It appears to be within 2 feet.' Three of the four transformers (T1, T2, T4) are documented as being within 2 feet of sidewalks, which meets or may slightly exceed the 2-foot minimum. T3 is within 2-5 feet. No specific dimension lines, callouts, or clearance annotations are provided on the site plan to document compliance with the 2-foot setback requirement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies: 'Transformer equipment pads not minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks.' The 'back of sidewalk' refers to the edge of the sidewalk surface farthest from the roadway or pedestrian area - essentially the inner edge of the sidewalk adjacent to property features. A 2-foot minimum separation is required to: (1) provide space for sidewalk maintenance and repair, (2) prevent sidewalk deterioration from transformer vibration or equipment settling, (3) ensure pedestrians are not placed in direct proximity to electrical equipment, and (4) allow for minor adjustments in sidewalk alignment during maintenance. Vision analysis indicates T1, T2, and T4 are at or potentially at less than the 2-foot minimum. While T3 may be within acceptable range (2-5 feet is unclear - 'within 2 to 5 feet' could mean 2 feet or could mean 5 feet). The absence of specific dimension documentation on the site plan creates ambiguity. To comply with the requirement, applicants must affirmatively demonstrate the 2-foot setback is maintained. Estimated visual distances are insufficient for compliance verification.

findings.comment: Transformer equipment pads not minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks. Sidewalk shown immediately adjacent to transformer pad without documented minimum clearance.
applicableAreas: Westernmost transformer pad location on western property line near Building 1
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a concrete sidewalk labeled 'Construct 6\' Concrete Sidewalk' immediately to the west of the transformer pad marked 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)'. Vision analysis confirmed 'To the immediate west of the pad is a pathway labeled "Construct 6\' Concrete Sidewalk."' The exact distance between the transformer pad and the back of this sidewalk is not dimensioned on the plan. Visual estimation from the plan at scale 1" = 20' suggests the sidewalk is very close (potentially less than 2 feet) from the transformer pad.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires a minimum 2-foot clearance from transformer pads to the back of sidewalks. The site plan shows a sidewalk immediately adjacent to (west of) the transformer pad, but does not dimension the specific clearance. Visual inspection at plan scale suggests the clearance is minimal and potentially less than 2 feet.

findings.comment: Measure the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area on Sheet 21. If any transformer is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas, show bollard locations and spacing (sized to allow equipment door opening) on the Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), Site Plan (Sheet 9), and Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). If all transformers are more than 4 feet from parking/traffic areas, note this on the plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads but does not display bollard symbols or callouts. The checklist item specifically applies 'only when pad-mounted transformer is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas.' Transformers are not shown on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or other discipline plans, making it impossible to accurately measure distances from transformer pads to the nearest parking or traffic areas using the plans. Sheet 21 shows the site layout and parking areas, but without clear transformer locations and precise measurements marked, the 4-foot threshold cannot be verified from available evidence.
findings.reasoning: This item is conditionally applicable only if any of the 5 transformers are located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. While Sheet 21 shows both transformers and parking areas, the distance relationship is not explicitly annotated with dimensions. To verify whether bollards are required, the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area must be measured or explicitly noted on the plans. Without such measurements, the applicability cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Dimension the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking area or traffic lane to verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 requirement that pads be within 6 feet of parking/traffic for AE truck accessibility. If distances exceed 6 feet, provide written Austin Energy Design approval for alternative spacing.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations relative to parking and traffic areas
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 88 parking spaces (10 surface, 78 garage) and internal driveways. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads: one west of Buildings 1/2 adjacent to a driveway curve, one between Buildings 4 and 5 near parking/circulation, one between Buildings 6 and 7 near parking/circulation, and one west of Building 8 near the property line. Vision analysis indicates that transformers appear to be in close proximity to parking and traffic areas, but 'there are absolutely no dimensions shown on this sheet that quantify the relationship or distance between the proposed electrical facilities and the proposed buildings.' Distances from transformers to parking/traffic areas are not dimensioned.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that 'Equipment pads be located within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for AE truck accessibility (unless otherwise specified by AE Design).' This requirement ensures that AE vehicles can position themselves close enough to equipment for safe and efficient maintenance. The applicant must either: (1) demonstrate that equipment pads are within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas (with dimensions), or (2) provide written AE Design approval if different spacing is used. Neither has been provided. The lack of dimensions prevents verification of compliance.

findings.comment: Dimension the distance from each transformer pad to the back (furthest from street/building) of adjacent sidewalks to verify minimum 2-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.4. If any pad is less than 2 feet from sidewalk, redesign pad location.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations near sidewalks and pedestrian paths
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows concrete sidewalks and decomposed granite walkways throughout the site near the buildings and around the detention pond. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad locations. However, there are no dimension lines or text specifying the clearance distances from any transformer pad to the adjacent sidewalks or pedestrian paths.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that 'Equipment pads be located minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks.' This requirement provides space for sidewalk maintenance and prevents equipment from interfering with pedestrian circulation. Without dimensioned drawings, the applicant has not demonstrated that this minimum 2-foot clearance is maintained at all transformer locations. Visual proximity does not constitute dimensional compliance verification.

findings.comment: Distances from transformer pads to drivable surfaces not dimensionally verified on plans, and laydown curb specifications not shown. Provide dimensioned measurements confirming distances from each transformer pad to nearest drivable surface, and if distances exceed 6 feet, provide laydown curb details with minimum 12-foot width and adequate load capacity specifications.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads adjacent to driveways where distances exceed 6 feet
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. All four transformer pads are shown adjacent to paved driveways within approximately 6 feet based on visual scale (1" = 20'). However, specific measurement dimensions are not labeled on the plans. Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad labeled "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" in a landscaped island between a sidewalk and drive aisle curb. No laydown curb specifications, dimensions, or details are shown on any sheet. No notes or details indicate whether laydown curbs are provided or what their specifications are (width, height, load capacity).
findings.reasoning: Code requires laydown curbs when transformer pads are not within 6 feet of drivable surface, with minimum 12-foot width and load capacity for transformer truck loads. The site plan shows transformers adjacent to driveways but does not explicitly measure the distances or confirm they are within 6 feet. More importantly, no laydown curb specifications are shown if any are required. Without clear dimensional verification of distances and explicit design details for any laydown curbs (including 12-foot minimum width and load capacity specifications), compliance cannot be determined. The exact location relationship of pads to curbs and drivable surfaces is ambiguous without precise measurements.

findings.comment: Transformer pad 2 is positioned less than 2 feet from a surface parking space, triggering the bollard requirement per UCM § 1.10.4. No bollards are shown on the electrical or site plans. Provide: (1) Detail drawing for 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards (per UCM § 1.10.4 standard specification) positioned around Transformer 2, with spacing adequate to allow equipment door openings and access (minimum 3-foot clear width for door swing), OR (2) Reposition Transformer 2 to a location more than 4 feet from all parking spaces and traffic areas.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 2 (eastern location, between Bldg. 4 and 5, adjacent to parking)
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 21 and 9 to identify transformer pad locations and proximity to parking areas. Transformer 2 (eastern side, between Bldg. 4 and 5) is positioned immediately adjacent to a surface parking space with less than 2 feet of separation per vision analysis: 'T2 is located directly adjacent to a perpendicular surface parking space. It appears to share a boundary or sit mere inches from the northernmost parking space in the cluster west of Bldg. 5. It is absolutely within 6 feet of this parking space.' No bollard symbols or notations are shown on Sheet 21 or Sheet 9 at this transformer location. Sheet 22 (Construction Details 1) was not reviewed but would be the expected location for bollard specifications if they were required and shown elsewhere on the plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies: 'Bollard requirement when transformer pad is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas... 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards are required and must be spaced to allow equipment door opening.' When transformer equipment is installed less than or equal to 4 feet from a parking space or traffic area, bollards must be provided to prevent vehicles from striking and damaging the transformer. Transformer 2 is less than 2 feet from a parking space, well within the 4-foot trigger distance. This proximity to parking makes the transformer vulnerable to vehicle impact and also creates a safety hazard for parked vehicles in an adjacent space that is separated only by the thin equipment pad. Bollards serve a dual purpose: (1) protecting the transformer from vehicle damage, and (2) preventing vehicles from parking or maneuvering too close to the electrical equipment. The absence of bollards at T2 violates this requirement.

findings.comment: Show drivable access routes from the nearest parking/traffic area to each transformer pad, with dimensions indicating the distance. If distance exceeds 6 feet, show the dedicated access route design.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) do not show drivable access routes to the transformer pad locations. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows transformers but does not indicate how Austin Energy trucks would access them for installation and maintenance. The grouping guidance specifies: 'Equipment pads must be located within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for Austin Energy truck accessibility unless otherwise approved by AE Design.' Without showing access routes, it cannot be verified that the transformer pads are accessible.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, pad-mounted transformers require drivable access routes for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. If a transformer is located more than 6 feet from an existing parking or traffic area, a dedicated access route must be provided and documented on the plans. Showing transformer locations without indicating access routes creates ambiguity about whether Austin Energy can reach the equipment for installation, operation, and maintenance.

findings.comment: Measure and show the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking/traffic area. If any pad is within 4 feet, show bollard locations and spacing (minimum 4-inch galvanized rigid metal posts) designed to allow equipment door opening.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pad locations but does not indicate distances to adjacent parking or driveway areas, nor are any bollards shown. No dimensions are provided that would allow verification of whether transformer pads are within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas or outside this distance. Vision analysis confirms: 'There is no indication of dedicated electrical clearance zones, specific electrical maintenance access routes, or bollard locations protecting the electrical equipment.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.10.4, when pad-mounted transformers are located within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas, 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards are required, spaced to allow equipment door opening. Bollards protect the equipment from vehicle damage. Without measuring distances from transformer pads to parking areas and showing required bollards, it cannot be verified that the site design protects equipment or meets code requirements.
